title: Continue Operating Card
summary: Configure Continue agents with explicit models, rules, tools, secrets, and a reproducible workspace-level verification loop.

sections.title: Use configuration as a reviewed agent contract
paragraphs: Continue agents combine models, rules, and tools through local or shared configuration. Choose it when you want an IDE or CLI workflow whose model and behavior can be configured independently of a single provider.
Treat imported blocks, documentation indexes, and MCP tools as dependencies. Review their source, permissions, data path, and update policy before enabling them.

sections.title: Keep rules versioned and credentials external
paragraphs: Place project rules in the documented workspace location and version them with the repository. Resolve the effective configuration before work so global, saved, and command-specific values do not silently change the task.
Reference secrets through the supported secret mechanism. Test the agent on a small representative change and verify the resulting diff and checks independently.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence includes the effective config, rule files, enabled tools, chosen model, reviewed diff, and test output. Verify that shared blocks and MCP servers stayed within their stated authority.
If behavior changes unexpectedly, return to the last reviewed config, disable newly introduced blocks or tools, restore the affected files, and repeat the same case.

sections.title: First Continue task: repair a CSV row validator
paragraphs: You will use Continue to inspect and propose a small Python change. The program validates a CSV file with the exact header `name,age,email`, a nonempty name of at most 40 characters, an integer age from 0 through 120 inclusive, and a simple email pattern. You will run four offline tests before and after reviewing a proposed change.

Use Continue IDE Chat or Edit with the local Ollama configuration described below. The Python tests use only the standard library. A model response, proposed diff, or passing test result does not authorize commit or deployment. Review the changed file and run the tests independently.

code.label: Task card
code.code:
Outcome: repair csv_validator.py so all four tests pass
Workspace: continue-csv-lab/
Initial files: csv_validator.py, test_csv_validator.py, malformed.csv
Change scope: csv_validator.py only
Model example: Ollama provider, qwen2.5-coder:7b tag
Interaction: Chat or Edit, followed by manual review and test execution
Secrets: none in files; never paste credentials into prompts
Verification: inspect the diff, then run python -m unittest -v test_csv_validator.py
Recovery: stop the active tool and restore only the scoped file from the reviewed reference or checkpoint
External effects: Python tests are offline; model calls and client bootstrap may use network or credits

sections.title: Create the first-task files without overwriting anything
paragraphs: Run the setup script from a parent directory in which you are allowed to create a new folder. It refuses to overwrite any existing file. Before writing, it checks every file destination, including nested rule and configuration paths. If any destination already exists, choose another root directory. The script does not remove, reset, or clean files.

The configuration file is included as a named CLI configuration exercise. An arbitrary `.continue/qwen-local.yaml` file is not assumed to be automatically discoverable by the IDE. Later instructions explain how to merge its model entry manually into the existing user configuration.

code.label: setup_continue_csv_lab.py
code.code:
from pathlib import Path
import sys

FILES = {
    "csv_validator.py": '''import csv
import re

EXPECTED_FIELDS = ["name", "age", "email"]
EMAIL = re.compile(r"[^@]+@[^@]+")


def validate(path):
    errors = []
    with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        reader = csv.DictReader(handle)
        if reader.fieldnames is None or set(reader.fieldnames) != set(EXPECTED_FIELDS):
            errors.append("line 1: header must be name,age,email")
        for line_number, row in enumerate(reader, start=2):
            name = (row.get("name") or "").strip()
            age_text = (row.get("age") or "").strip()
            email = (row.get("email") or "").strip()
            if not name:
                errors.append(f"line {line_number}: name is required")
            elif len(name) > 40:
                errors.append(f"line {line_number}: name is too long")
            try:
                age = int(age_text)
                if age > 120:
                    raise ValueError
            except ValueError:
                errors.append(f"line {line_number}: age must be an integer from 0 through 120")
            if not EMAIL.fullmatch(email):
                errors.append(f"line {line_number}: email is invalid")
    return errors
''',
    "test_csv_validator.py": '''import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from csv_validator import validate


class CsvValidatorTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def write_csv(self, text):
        handle = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="w", newline="", encoding="utf-8", delete=False)
        self.addCleanup(lambda: Path(handle.name).unlink(missing_ok=True))
        handle.write(text)
        handle.close()
        return handle.name

    def test_valid_row(self):
        path = self.write_csv("name,age,email\\nAda Lovelace,36,ada@example.com\\n")
        self.assertEqual(validate(path), [])

    def test_exact_header_order_is_required(self):
        path = self.write_csv("age,name,email\\n36,Ada Lovelace,ada@example.com\\n")
        self.assertIn("line 1: header must be name,age,email", validate(path))

    def test_negative_age_is_rejected(self):
        path = self.write_csv("name,age,email\\nAda Lovelace,-1,ada@example.com\\n")
        self.assertIn("line 2: age must be an integer from 0 through 120", validate(path))

    def test_malformed_row_values_are_reported(self):
        path = self.write_csv("name,age,email\\n,abc,not-an-email\\n")
        errors = validate(path)
        self.assertEqual(len(errors), 3)
        self.assertIn("line 2: name is required", errors)
        self.assertIn("line 2: age must be an integer from 0 through 120", errors)
        self.assertIn("line 2: email is invalid", errors)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
''',
    "malformed.csv": "name,age,email\n,abc,not-an-email\n",
    ".continue/qwen-local.yaml": '''name: qwen-local
version: 1.0.0
schema: v1
models:
  - name: Qwen local coding
    provider: ollama
    model: qwen2.5-coder:7b
    apiBase: http://localhost:11434
    roles:
      - chat
      - edit
      - apply
''',
    ".continue/rules/csv-lab.md": '''# CSV lab rule

Work only on the requested CSV validator change. Preserve unrelated edits.
Use Python 3 standard-library code. Explain proposed edits before applying them.
Do not add packages, credentials, network services, or generated files.
Run the named unit test after editing and report failures without claiming that a
model or tool ran a command unless the user actually observed that command.
''',
}

root = Path(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else Path("continue-csv-lab")
root = root.resolve()
targets = [root / relative for relative in FILES]
existing = [target for target in targets if target.exists()]
if existing:
    names = "\n".join(str(target) for target in existing)
    raise FileExistsError("Refusing to overwrite these destinations:\n" + names)
root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
for target in targets:
    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
for relative, content in FILES.items():
    target = root / relative
    target.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8", newline="")
    print(f"created {target}")
print(f"Lab created at {root}")

sections.title: Configure Ollama and Continue without guessing IDE controls
paragraphs: The YAML entry uses provider `ollama`, model tag `qwen2.5-coder:7b`, and `http://localhost:11434`, with `chat`, `edit`, and `apply` roles. The tag is a sourced example, not a recommendation or compatibility guarantee. Run `ollama list` and compare the complete tag exactly before diagnosing a connection problem. Continue's Ollama guide says the configured tag must match an installed tag and documents this API base. Source: https://docs.continue.dev/guides/ollama-guide, observed 2026-09-20.

Continue configuration requires `name`, `version`, and `schema`; model entries require `name`, `provider`, and `model`. Declaring roles does not prove that the model supports native tool use. This task uses Chat or Edit plus manual review and test commands, so native Agent tool support is not required. Source: https://docs.continue.dev/reference, observed 2026-09-20.

For VS Code, open the Continue sidebar with Ctrl+L on Windows or Linux, or Cmd+L on macOS. Use the gear associated with the agent selector above the input, then use the documented Local Config cog to open the existing user `config.yaml`. On Windows, this is under the user profile's `.continue/config.yaml`; on other systems it is under `~/.continue/config.yaml`. Manually merge the `models` entry from `.continue/qwen-local.yaml`, preserving all existing settings and entries. Save the user configuration so Continue refreshes it. Do not use an overwrite script and do not assume the project YAML is automatically selectable. Source: https://docs.continue.dev/customize/deep-dives/configuration, observed 2026-09-20.

The project rule is at `.continue/rules/csv-lab.md` and can be versioned with the repository. Rules guide Agent, Chat, and Edit behavior, but natural-language rules are not filesystem or shell security boundaries. Source: https://docs.continue.dev/customize/rules, observed 2026-09-20.

If you use the CLI, run `cn --version` and record its actual output. Do not copy a version from this exercise and do not label an example as observed.

sections.title: Request a scoped Chat or Edit change
paragraphs: Use Chat to request a proposed patch, or use Edit and inspect the proposed change before applying it. Ask for changes only in `csv_validator.py`. Do not ask the client to commit, deploy, install packages, change permissions, or edit the tests. If the proposal touches another file, stop and request a narrower proposal.

sections.title: Review the expected corrected source and result
paragraphs: A correct minimal repair compares `reader.fieldnames` directly with the expected ordered list and rejects ages below zero as well as ages above 120. Python's `csv.DictReader.fieldnames` preserves header order, which is why a set comparison is insufficient. Source: https://docs.python.org/3/library/csv.html#csv.DictReader, observed 2026-09-20.

The following is the complete authored reference source. It is not a claim that Continue or Ollama generated or applied it. After reviewing an equivalent diff, run the tests yourself. The expected result is four passing tests and unchanged tests.

sections.title: Diagnose configuration, permission, and code failures
paragraphs: If Ollama returns a missing-model response such as 404, stop the active Continue generation first. Run `ollama list`, compare the complete configured tag, and use only an approved exact installed tag in a separately reviewed configuration. Do not silently substitute a model or put credentials in YAML. The Ollama guide documents the exact-tag requirement and the missing-tag failure. Source: https://docs.continue.dev/guides/ollama-guide, observed 2026-09-20.

If the wrong configuration loaded, stop the active tool, verify the project directory and the explicit `--config` path if using the CLI, and inspect the selected file. Do not use a wildcard allow rule to resolve uncertainty. A local model endpoint does not prove that the whole client is offline.

CLI permissions distinguish `allow` for automatic execution, `ask` for TUI approval, and `exclude` for hiding a tool. Write, Edit, MultiEdit, and Bash default to `ask`; headless mode excludes ask tools. `--exclude Bash` hides the terminal tool, while read-only tools can include network-capable Fetch. Source: https://docs.continue.dev/cli/tool-permissions, observed 2026-09-20.

If an edit regresses the code, stop the active tool before recovery. Preserve unrelated edits and restore only `csv_validator.py` from the reviewed reference or a known checkpoint. Rerun the test command and inspect the diff. Restoring a file cannot undo external effects such as network requests, model charges, or actions already performed by an external tool.

python -m unittest -v test_csv_validator.py

# Optional diagnostic session with terminal hidden. Not a repair command.

sections.title: Independent changed-input task: create a separate folder first
paragraphs: Before reading the feedback section, create a separate folder named `continue-csv-lab-independent`. Do not modify the original folder. The setup below creates a complete independent copy with the first task's corrected three-column source and a protected four-column test suite. It preflights every destination before writing and refuses to overwrite anything.

The independent contract materially changes the requirements: the exact header is `name,age,email,country`; age must be 18 through 65 inclusive; country must be nonempty after stripping and no more than two characters. The protected tests cover a valid row, both age boundaries, rejection of 17 and 66, a blank country, the old header, malformed values, and the existing name and email rules. Do not weaken or copy the original test methods unchanged.

import sys

FILES = {
    "csv_validator.py": '''import csv
import re

EXPECTED_FIELDS = ["name", "age", "email"]
EMAIL = re.compile(r"[^@]+@[^@]+")


def validate(path):

    with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        reader = csv.DictReader(handle)
        if reader.fieldnames != EXPECTED_FIELDS:
            errors.append("line 1: header must be name,age,email")
        for line_number, row in enumerate(reader, start=2):
            name = (row.get("name") or "").strip()
            age_text = (row.get("age") or "").strip()
            email = (row.get("email") or "").strip()
            if not name:
                errors.append(f"line {line_number}: name is required")
            elif len(name) > 40:
                errors.append(f"line {line_number}: name is too long")
            try:
                age = int(age_text)
                if age < 0 or age > 120:
                    raise ValueError
            except ValueError:
                errors.append(f"line {line_number}: age must be an integer from 0 through 120")
            if not EMAIL.fullmatch(email):
                errors.append(f"line {line_number}: email is invalid")
    return errors
''',
    "test_csv_validator.py": '''import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from csv_validator import validate


class IndependentCsvValidatorTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def write_csv(self, text):
        handle = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="w", newline="", encoding="utf-8", delete=False)
        self.addCleanup(lambda: Path(handle.name).unlink(missing_ok=True))
        handle.write(text)
        handle.close()
        return handle.name

    def test_valid_adult_row(self):
        path = self.write_csv("name,age,email,country\\nGrace Hopper,36,grace@example.com,US\\n")
        self.assertEqual(validate(path), [])

    def test_age_18_is_accepted(self):

sections.title: Attempt the changed requirement before reading feedback
paragraphs: Run the protected independent suite from `continue-csv-lab-independent` before asking Continue for help. The starting source still validates the original three-column contract, so failures should expose the causal mismatch. Ask Continue to edit only the independent `csv_validator.py`; do not edit the protected tests or the original folder.

Use the exact key `adult-range-and-header` when you are ready to reveal the feedback. Your prompt should require the four-column header, country validation, and the inclusive adult age range. Run the copied test suite after reviewing any proposed diff.

Key: adult-range-and-header

Update only csv_validator.py in this independent folder.

Requirements:
1. Require the exact header name,age,email,country.
2. Preserve the name and email requirements and error strings.
3. Require an integer age from 18 through 65 inclusive.
4. Require a nonempty stripped country of at most 2 characters.

6. Use only Python 3 standard-library code.

Explain how the changed schema affects the header comparison and row lookups. Show a proposed diff before any edit. Do not claim tests ran unless their output is visible to me.

sections.title: Causal feedback after the independent attempt
paragraphs: Reveal this section only after attempting the independent task and running its protected tests. The key is `adult-range-and-header`. The schema changed from three columns to four, so the exact header constant, country row lookup, country validation, and expected header error must change together. The age predicate must change from `0 <= age <= 120` to `18 <= age <= 65`; changing only one endpoint is incomplete.

The independent suite deliberately asserts exact complete error strings, including the `line 2: ` prefix. Assertions must search for those complete strings in the returned error list. Do not use unprefixed fragments such as `"country is required" in errors`, because that cannot pass when the implementation correctly includes the line prefix.

The original source and original reference are not solutions for this task. If the changed tests fail while the source still has the original constants, that is causal evidence that the new requirement was not propagated through the implementation. Keep the original three-column exercise untouched.

sections.title: Capture observed evidence and preserve boundaries
paragraphs: For a real run, record the date, workspace path, actual Continue extension version, exact configuration path, model tag shown by `ollama list`, interaction type, proposed or applied files, reviewed diff, exact test command, and exact output. Redact tokens, API keys, authorization headers, private URLs, and personal data. Record an approval only if an approval was actually shown.

The fictional example below is deliberately labeled and must not be reported as observed: `FICTIONAL EXAMPLE, not observed: I selected the local configuration, the model proposed changes only to csv_validator.py, I reviewed the diff, and the test command reported four tests OK.` Local Python tests do not establish that Continue bootstrap, model calls, or other client tools were offline.
Before commit, compare the final diff with the requested scope and rerun the tests. Passing tests are evidence about tested behavior, not authorization to commit or deploy.

sections.title: ASSUMPTIONS
paragraphs: The learner has Python 3, a supported Continue client, permission to create new local directories, and an Ollama installation if choosing the local model route. The operating system, IDE version, Continue extension version, Ollama version, installed tags, endpoint reachability, and model tool capability are not established here.

The supplied official documentation findings were observed on 2026-09-20. Configuration snippets are exercise inputs and documented shapes, not evidence of a live backend, installed model, successful authentication, or successful client execution. The learner may have unrelated repository edits, so the procedure uses separate folders and scoped file changes.

sections.title: OMITTED
paragraphs: No live Continue, IDE, Ollama, model call, permission approval, network state, test run, generated patch, or current extension or Ollama version is claimed. No price, guaranteed model capability, or credential-free startup behavior is supplied because those facts were not established.

The independent task intentionally requires an attempt before revealing its answer implementation. The complete runnable answer is supplied afterward, together with protected tests and causal feedback.
